title: Reverse Linked List II
statement_short: Given the head of a singly linked list and two integers left and right where left <= right, reverse the nodes of the list from position left to position right in-place and return the updated list.
hint: Small n does not limit time complexity, but sub-list reversal requires O(1) auxiliary space pointer manipulation.
why_not: Right: Two Pointers (prev, curr, and position pointers) traverse to the left boundary and reverse nodes in-place in O(n) time and O(1) space. Not Stack: Pushing nodes from position left to right onto a stack reverses their order but uses O(right - left) extra space. Not 1D DP: Dynamic programming subproblem caching is unnecessary for pointer manipulation. Not HashMap / Hash Set: Mapping node indices in a hash map uses unnecessary auxiliary memory.
